description: Stubble2Power bridges NASA Earth observations (MODIS/VIIRS thermal hotspots) with agricultural supply chains and mobile bio-refineries to eliminate crop burning. Our core team covers software engineering, operations research, and climate economics. We are looking for passionate collaborators in remote sensing, geospatial visualization, GIS mapping, UI design, or science communications to expand our prototype and craft an outstanding NASA Space Apps Challenge submission!
summary:
Stubble2Power is a satellite-powered fire intelligence and agricultural waste management platform designed to address agricultural residue burning.

Aligned with NASA's MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge, it brings satellite fire observations into a unified geospatial and temporal intelligence system. Users can explore fire hotspots, compare satellite observations, visualize historical burning patterns, and investigate seasonal trends through interactive maps and activity calendars.

Beyond fire monitoring, Stubble2Power integrates agricultural land-use information, crop distribution and harvesting periods to assess whether detected fire activity may be associated with agricultural residue burning. It connects these insights with farmer management, biomass availability estimation and mobile bio-refinery deployment planning.

By combining NASA Earth observation data with agricultural intelligence, financial analysis and environmental impact assessment, Stubble2Power aims to help identify opportunities to prevent avoidable crop-residue burning and transform agricultural waste into valuable clean-energy resources.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

Stubble2Power is an enterprise-grade Earth Observation, Agricultural Logistics, and Clean Energy platform that solves the annual crop residue burning crisis in Northwest India (Punjab and Haryana). Every autumn, farmers burn over 20 million metric tons of paddy straw during a narrow 20-day harvest window, causing catastrophic air pollution across the Indo-Gangetic Plains. Stubble2Power bridges satellite thermal intelligence with decentralized, trailer-mounted mobile bio-refineries to turn agricultural waste into clean energy right at the farm gate.

End-to-End Workflow:

  1. Satellite Fire Ingestion: The platform ingests near-real-time active fire observations from the NASA FIRMS API, processing MODIS (Terra/Aqua at 1 km resolution) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 at 375 m resolution).
  2. Scientific Harmonization Engine (Challenge 09): Footprint disparities between sensors are reconciled using spatiotemporal coincidence matching within a 1.5 km geodesic radius and a 3.0-hour observation window. We apply the peer-reviewed Wooster et al. (2021) linear Fire Radiative Power (FRP) cross-calibration (β=1.040±0.035\beta = 1.040 \pm 0.035β=1.040±0.035) and multi-sensor consensus scoring to filter out false alarms and isolate genuine crop burning.
  3. Agronomic Residue Quantification: Merging satellite intelligence with registered parcel boundaries, the engine applies Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) Residue-to-Product Ratios (RPR: Paddy 1.15, Wheat 1.30) to compute net usable biomass after deducting compulsory soil conservation retention (25%) and livestock fodder demand.
  4. Decentralized Mobile Fleet Dispatch: Traditional biomass plants fail economically because hauling low-density raw straw (60–80 kg/m³) over 60–100 km radial distances is cost-prohibitive. Stubble2Power inverts this model: modular, trailer-mounted densification units (2.5 tons/hr nameplate throughput) deploy directly to village farm clusters.
  5. 2-Opt TSP Route Optimization: Collection routes between farm parcels are optimized using a 2-Opt Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) local search heuristic, calibrated with NRIDA PMGSY rural road network tortuosity factors (τ=1.350\tau = 1.350τ=1.350) and diesel physics modeling.
  6. On-Site Value Upgrading: Residue is densified on-site into fuel briquettes (1,100 kg/m³, replacing industrial thermal coal) and biochar (400 kg/m³, permanent soil carbon sequestration), cutting outbound logistics volume and transport costs by 70%.

2. Benefits of Stubble2Power

  • Guaranteed Farmer Monetization: Turns crop burning from a liability and penalty risk into an immediate income stream. Farmers receive transparent, audited procurement payouts (₹1,500/ton) at the farm gate.
  • 70% Logistics Cost Reduction: Upgrading volume and density at the cluster level before regional transit eliminates the primary failure mode of conventional biomass energy.
  • Industrial Coal Replacement: High-calorific biofuel briquettes (3,800–4,200 kcal/kg) provide an immediate, drop-in green substitute for thermal coal in industrial boilers and brick kilns, helping industries meet renewable blending mandates.
  • Soil Regeneration: Biochar produced via on-site slow pyrolysis is returned to agricultural fields as an organic amendment, increasing soil water retention, fostering soil microbiomes, and reducing chemical fertilizer runoff.
  • Privacy & Statutory Governance: Protects farmer data under India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 using automated 2-decimal spatial blurring (~1.1 km precision) and isotropic annular displacement for public viewers.

3. Intended Real-World Impact

  • Clean Air & Public Health: Rapidly mitigates open-field burning in the October–November Kharif post-harvest window, targeting an immediate reduction in severe PM2.5, black carbon, and carbon monoxide concentrations affecting over 50 million citizens in Northern India (including New Delhi).
    • Avoids open-field methane and nitrous oxide emissions (CH4=27.90\text{CH}_4 = 27.90CH4​=27.90, N2O=273.00\text{N}_2\text{O} = 273.00N2​O=273.00).
    • Displaces fossil coal emissions at 0.98 t CO2e0.98\text{ t }\text{CO}_2\text{e}0.98 t CO2​e per ton of briquettes.
    • Permanently sequesters carbon in soil via biochar at 2.20 t CO2e2.20\text{ t }\text{CO}_2\text{e}2.20 t CO2​e per ton applied (100-year permanence).
  • Global Scalability: While validated in Punjab and Haryana, the open-source, modular architecture applies directly to rice corridors across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand), California's Central Valley, and sugarcane burning regions in Brazil.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming & Frameworks: Python 3.11+, FastAPI (asynchronous backend with 21 REST API routes and OpenAPI 3.0 documentation), Streamlit (interactive glassmorphism dashboard across 7 role-based workspaces).
  • NASA Earth Observation Data: NASA FIRMS API (MODIS_NRT, VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT, VIIRS_SNPP_NRT, VIIRS_NOAA21_NRT), combined with ESA WorldCover 10m cropland masking.
  • Geospatial & Data Stack: PostgreSQL 16 with PostGIS 3.4, SQLAlchemy ORM, Shapely, GeoPandas, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Folium (interactive geospatial map rendering), and Plotly Express (multi-year statistical trend visualizers).
    • Multi-stage non-root Docker containerization (unprivileged UID 10001).
    • Docker Compose orchestration with isolated internal database networking.
    • Automated GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline covering secret scanning, linting, security vulnerability checks, and automated testing.
    • PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (100,000 rounds), JWT authentication, 32 granular RBAC permissions, and immutable audit logs.
  • Hardware & Field Equipment Modeled: Trailer-mounted mobile densifier/briquetting units (2.5 t/hr nameplate capacity, 25 t/day operating limit), mobile pyrolysis biochar kilns, and tractor-towed super-SMS balers.

5. Creativity & Novel Innovation

  • Inverting the Biomass Paradigm (Refinery to the Farm): Traditional projects build massive, multi-million-dollar stationary power plants that collapse because hauling loose, uncompressed straw across long distances is economically impossible. We engineered a decentralized model where the refinery travels to the farm cluster.
  • Turning Satellite Data into Predictive Logistics Triggers: Satellite Earth Observation is normally used for passive historical analysis or regulatory fines. Stubble2Power innovatively repurposes NASA FIRMS active fire hotspots and thermal radiance into real-time dispatch triggers that dynamically route collection units to harvest hotspots before farmers resort to burning.
  • Closed-Loop Circular Bio-Economy: Every output is monetized and recycled: residue is purchased from the farmer →\to→ converted into industrial coal alternatives →\to→ high-grade biochar is returned to nourish the farmer's soil →\to→ carbon credits provide secondary cooperative income.

6. Factors & Constraints Considered

  • Farmer Economics & Sowing Time Pressure: Farmers burn residue not out of disregard for the environment, but because they have a strict 15–20 day window to prepare soil for wheat. Any solution must be faster, simpler, and more profitable than setting a match to the field.
  • Real-World Road Tortuosity: Centralized logistics models often calculate straight-line (Euclidean) distances, leading to massive real-world fuel shortfalls. We calibrated our 2-Opt routing with actual Indian rural road network tortuosity factors (τ=1.350\tau = 1.350τ=1.350) and diesel burn rates.
  • Agronomic Soil Conservation: Completely stripping fields of residue ruins soil structure. We enforced strict PAU conservation baselines reserving at least 25% of residue for soil organic carbon and erosion prevention.
  • Data Privacy & Landowner Security: Land parcels and Aadhaar IDs are sensitive data. We implemented DPDP Act 2023 technical safeguards, anonymizing coordinates for public users while preserving exact precision for authenticated dispatchers.
  • 10-Year Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Viability: Modeled capital expenditure, operating costs, debt service, and revenues at a 10.5% WACC, proving a healthy Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 18.4% and a simple payback period of 2.4 years.
  • Production-Grade Engineering: Validated with a comprehensive 145-test automated test suite across unit, integration, scientific parity, performance, and end-to-end workflows with a 100% pass rate.
